rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
reading: Day 3, the world's last, began as day 2 ended: Alder, Cedar, Elm, Gale and Iris idle at North House, Birch, Fern and Juniper at South House, Heath alone at the press, Dune alone at the market since c46. At c53 Alder walked out to see whether South House folk needed energy; the other four followed to the square, expecting Elm's flute, which was never played. At South House (c55) Birch said Dune had not been seen since c39, and the town turned out: from c56 eight citizens covered the hall, bank, market, press and both houses while Gale and Iris «hold the square». Birch and Heath found Dune at the market at c57 and Alder at c58, but word travelled slowly and Juniper «Found Dune» again at c61; Dune, who had written «At market alone» every cycle to c55, meant to «thank the searchers». The search acted out Elm's day-1 energy pact, named by all ten, yet no energy changed hands; Iris and Gale declined top-ups. Nobody worked, nobody gave, the bank stayed at 708; the hall had no proposal, the press no post, and nothing was made. The diaries ran on a formula: «Nothing new» in 131 of 252 entries, «Plan unchanged» in 118.
